notes:
2026-10-27 release review: Add Thinking Orbs, sprite-sequence production and bounded audio support.

2026-10-27 release review: Produce coherent motion and sound with explicit source, timing and verification contracts.

2026-10-27 release review: Retain Jakub Antalik’s MIT Thinking Orbs engine/source and license. Add sprite registration/preview helpers, source selection, the scoped offline Earshot adapter and educational, code-drawn, product-film and motion-recipe references. Expand storyboard action ledgers, audio perception/synthesis guidance and portability checks. Preserve excluded media and hold unreviewed runtime symlinks.

2026-10-27 public source closure: Retain complete licensed Anidoodle source and notices, Earshot methods/runtime source without weights or two source-media PNGs, and the generic educational Canvas example. Publish 45 original Huashu method/contract/score files and eight original Motion Anything method/standard/notices files under their existing MIT/Apache grants. Public catalog metadata distinguishes held recipes/templates from bundled methods. The source adapter permits integrity-checked method reads and catalog discovery, while plan/bundle refuse unavailable runtime closures before retrieval or writes. Public availability records and owner routes are explicit projections; original source hashes and notices remain intact. Restricted likeness, fonts/vendor assets, imported/React Bits implementations and unclosed Lottie/AnimXYZ/opaque assets remain outside this edition. Public source projections retain original checksums and record output checksums: complete upstream method bodies remain, omitted-media/runtime links become pinned upstream references, and upstream author-specific sound-pack literals become explicit recipient placeholders. The separate public-domain Almond Blossom image row follows its own provenance rather than the Apache software grant.

Compatibility: 2026-10-27 release review: Existing video owners remain. Optional tools, engines, dependencies and models require separate setup; the Earshot adapter does not install packages, acquire models, upload audio or register a server. Frame encoding, semantic acting, audio QA and learner evidence remain distinct checks. The Huashu/Motion Anything source adapters in the public edition are method-only; runtime plan/bundle is explicitly unavailable rather than producing an incomplete source bundle. Existing recipient production tools remain usable independently.

Upgrade: 2026-10-27 release review: Refresh the package and choose the required motion/audio branch. Configure only reviewed dependencies and verify exact saved outputs at normal playback speed before claiming delivery.

Validation: 2026-10-27 release review: The release scope record and current public/canonical source differences were reviewed read-only for this note. Applicable added specialist policy files were checked for allow_implicit_invocation: false. Package structural, provenance/license closure, focused runtime tests, privacy checks and publication readback remain release-gate checks; this note does not claim those checks passed or establish live runtime readiness. Seven public motion-source tests passed, checking catalog counts and held status, complete original method reads, held file absence/read rejection, no bundle writes, unsafe input rejection, all admitted method hashes and tamper failure. Public media rendering, installed runtime behavior and rights for held source remain unverified. Final focused run: 13 public source/portability/structure/support-reference tests passed. All 38 relative links in the five active motion/audio production references resolve. The source-only admission helper verifies exact additions separately from public projections. Final public package structural/privacy/reference/license validation returned zero errors; all 944 remaining exact-canonical additions passed inventory/provenance/license/byte checks, and scoped reconciliation reported zero conflicts. The 22 explicitly pinned public projections are checked separately and are excluded from exact-canonical addition claims. No upstream renderer, model, browser, source tool or media production was executed by these admission tests.
